lines: A pale blue yukata with flower petals — in this whole world
I think you're probably the one it suits best
I actually managed to ask you out — I could cry
The last day of the summer festival, you melting cotton candy in your mouth
You tell me, wanting to be that cotton candy myself, "This is fun"
I just nod — no clever words come out at all
I'm not used to walking beside you, and the embarrassment of it
If this longing overflows, how
on what occasion, at what moment
am I supposed to take your hand?
Your hand that looks soft no matter how I see it —
with how much strength do I hold it
and with what expression should I gaze at you?
The song you were humming a moment ago
and the times our eyes meet now and then —
there's no deep meaning behind them, right?
It's sad, but
just you smiling at me — that alone, and at last I
found where my heart belongs: noisy, aching, frustrating
If this longing overflows, how
on what occasion, at what moment
am I supposed to take your hand?
Your hand that looks soft no matter how I see it —
with how much strength do I hold it
and with what expression should I gaze at you?
The fireworks are going up soon, aren't they
I stare at your profile now, as if to burn it into memory
This ache in my chest — how
am I supposed to pass it on to you?
Just being beside you isn't enough
Some topic that could catch your interest —
I ran out of those long ago
The words left to me, I know
I know, but
If this longing overflows, how
on what occasion, at what moment
am I supposed to take your hand?
Your hand that looks soft no matter how I see it —
with how much strength do I hold it
and with what expression should I gaze at you?
The last day of the summer festival — to you, melting cotton candy in your mouth,
I, wanting to be that cotton candy, say, "This is fun"
